status_definitions.supported: Evidence supports the stated direction, sign, and reasoning within the declared scope.
status_definitions.partially_supported: Evidence supports only part of the claim, a narrower population or outcome, or an association rather than the full causal claim.
status_definitions.contradicted: Relevant evidence opposes the claimed direction or sign within the declared scope.
status_definitions.mixed_evidence: Relevant evidence both supports and opposes the same defined claim.
status_definitions.insufficient_evidence: Available evidence does not establish or refute the causal claim.
status_definitions.not_assessable: Undefined variable coding or endpoint makes the proposed direction or sign uninterpretable.

methodology.scope: 1990_8 yo.py, 58 edges, using the four supplied PDF files and 25 saved PubMed HTML abstracts in 1990 ADHD Papers. Direction, sign, and written reasoning were reviewed; numeric strength was excluded.
methodology.age_scope: Evidence specific to children near age eight was preferred. Older-child and adolescent evidence was treated as partial when it did not report an age-eight estimate.
methodology.causal_standard: Associations, reviews, and clinical recommendations were not automatically treated as proof of causal direction. Undefined categorical signs were marked not_assessable.
methodology.source_limits: This is a validation against the supplied corpus, not a systematic review of all 1990 ADHD literature. A status of insufficient_evidence is not evidence that an edge is false.
methodology.strength: The graph's numeric edge strengths were not validated.
methodology.duplicate: No exact duplicate PDFs or duplicate PMID records were found. HTML pages are deduplicated by PMID; repeated sentences in an abstract are not independent findings.
methodology.html_scope: HTML evidence is restricted to the main English abstract of each saved record, excluding similar/cited articles. All 25 records are dated 1990. Abstract-only limitations are retained; the side-effect abstract (PMID 2196520) is marked truncated and repeats a passage.
methodology.adult_scope: The adult review (PMID 2251528) supplies clinical context, not a controlled treatment estimate or specific results at age 32 or 45. Pediatric findings are not transferred to adult graphs.

edges.existing_reasoning: Genetic liability contributes strongly to childhood ADHD.
edges.observation_from_validation: The blinded family study finds excess ADD among first-degree relatives after accounting for several measured factors. This adds family-genetic evidence, but does not isolate inherited effects from shared environment or establish the claim that genetic liability contributes strongly at exactly age eight.
edges.recommended_action: Retain familial/genetic liability as a qualified pathway; avoid a quantified strong genetic effect from family-history evidence alone.

evidence.exact_excerpt: These results confirm and extend previous findings indicating important family-genetic risk factors in ADD.
evidence.location: Family-genetic and psychosocial risk factors in DSM-III attention deficit disorder - PubMed.html; English abstract (#eng-abstract)
evidence.relevance: Blinded family study supports familial liability; shared environment is not fully separated and strong genetic causation or an exact-age effect is not established.

edges.existing_reasoning: Underlying ADHD increases symptom severity.
edges.observation_from_validation: ADHD and Symptom Severity overlap unless the disorder is defined separately from diagnostic symptoms.
edges.recommended_action: Define separate latent and measured constructs.

edges.existing_reasoning: Underlying ADHD shapes visible behavioral presentation.
edges.observation_from_validation: Symptom Type is categorical, so a universal positive sign is undefined.

edges.existing_reasoning: At age 8, symptoms are highly visible through behavior and school functioning.
edges.observation_from_validation: Children aged 8.6-12.11 showed poorer arithmetic discrepancy and more social withdrawal or uncommunicativeness than younger children, but the study was cross-sectional and did not validate general symptom severity.
edges.recommended_action: Replace the generic positive edge with specific age-by-outcome relationships and note the cross-sectional design.

edges.existing_reasoning: Medication can reduce child impairment.

edges.recommended_action: Retain as domain-specific benefit; distinguish classroom/on-task gains from learning, social functioning, and global impairment.
